issues.title: Undefined identifier True used instead
issues.description: The rule requires all TypeScript code to compile successfully with strict mode enabled. The code uses `True` (Python-style boolean) which is not a valid JavaScript/TypeScript identifier, causing a compilation error.
issues.rule_name: TypeScript Files Must Follow Strict TypeScript Configuration

issues.title: JSON schema not normalized before storage
issues.description: In the handleJSONSchemaChange callback, the code stores the raw user input value directly instead of the normalized JSON.stringify(v, null, 2) version. This means that if a user enters compact JSON like {"type":"object"}, it will be stored as-is rather than being formatted consistently. This breaks the intended behavior where all JSON schemas should be stored in a standardized pretty-printed format with 2-space indentation. When the schema is later retrieved and displayed, it may have inconsistent formatting, and downstream consumers expecting normalized JSON may encounter issues.

issues.title: JSON schema cleared for all variable types, not just jsonObject
issues.description: The payloadToSave logic removes the json_schema field whenever isSchemaEmpty is true, regardless of the variable type. The original code correctly checked `tempPayload.type === InputVarType.jsonObject && isSchemaEmpty`. By removing the type check, if a user switches from jsonObject type to another type (like textInput) and the schema happens to be empty, the json_schema field gets cleared even though it should be preserved during the transition. This causes data loss when users change variable types back and forth.

issues.title: JSON schema validation uses non-normalized value
issues.description: The validation logic for jsonObject type validates jsonSchemaValue instead of normalizedJsonSchema. This is problematic because normalizedJsonSchema is computed earlier and correctly handles the case where an empty schema should be undefined. By validating jsonSchemaValue directly, the code validates the raw tempPayload value instead of the cleaned version. This inconsistency means that validation may pass but the wrong data could be saved, or validation may fail when it should succeed if the schema is empty but not yet normalized.

issues.title: Dead store / unused variable `normalizedJsonSchema`
issues.description: SonarJS no-dead-store is enforced at error level. `normalizedJsonSchema` is assigned but never used afterwards, making it a dead store and a lint violation.
issues.rule_name: Frontend ESLint Sonarjs Rules Must Be Followed

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30412 - fix(web): enable JSON_OBJECT type support in console UI

structured_output.summary:
This PR exposes the `JSON_OBJECT` input type in the chatflow/workflow variable modal by removing the hard-coded `isSupportJSON = false` gate. It also changes the JSON Schema editor so it edits the full schema rather than only `properties`, and so the saved value is the schema string the user typed. `handleConfirm` gains validation: the schema must parse and must have `type: "object"`, and an empty schema is stored as `undefined`. The placeholder is updated to match, and i18n keys are added across 14 locales.

The direction is right and matches the backend, which already runs `Draft7Validator.check_schema` on `json_schema` in `api/core/app/app_config/entities.py`. However, `handleJSONSchemaChange` contains `return True`, which is not valid TypeScript and will fail type-checking and the production build. Invalid JSON typed into the editor is also silently dropped, so the new "invalid JSON" validation never fires. The PR adds no tests despite the checklist claiming them.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `True` identifier in `handleJSONSchemaChange` breaks the TypeScript build, which blocks merge on its own. Beyond that, the validation added in `handleConfirm` cannot reach the invalid-JSON case because the editor handler never writes invalid text into state, so users lose edits silently. Remaining items are lint-level unused locals, a dead export, and missing tests.

architecture.overview:
Input variables for advanced-chat and workflow apps are edited in `ConfigModal` (`web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/index.tsx`). The modal keeps a `tempPayload` state object of type `InputVar`, and `handleConfirm` passes it to `onConfirm`, which writes the variable into the app or workflow config. Before this PR the `JSON_OBJECT` option was gated behind a constant `isSupportJSON = false`, so the option never appeared. The JSON Schema editor showed only the `properties` sub-object and re-wrapped it into `{type:'object', properties, ...}` on every keystroke.

The PR removes the gate and makes the editor show and store the full schema string. It validates on confirm that the schema is JSON with `type: "object"`. On the backend, `VariableEntity.validate_json_schema` in `api/core/app/app_config/entities.py` already enforces Draft-7 validity, and `StartNode._validate_and_normalize_json_object_inputs` validates runtime inputs against the stored schema. The frontend change is therefore a UI-side exposure and validation pass; the runtime path is unchanged.
steps: Entry point: the user opens the variable modal for an advanced-chat or workflow app. `isBasicApp` controls whether the JSON option is listed in `selectOptions`.
`jsonSchemaStr` (index.tsx lines 81-91) pretty-prints the stored `json_schema` string and feeds it to the Monaco-backed `CodeEditor`.

`handleJSONSchemaChange` (lines 130-144) runs on every edit. It clears the field on empty input and writes the raw text into `tempPayload.json_schema`. Invalid JSON is ignored, so state keeps the last valid value.
`handleConfirm` (lines 248-329) normalizes the empty schema to `undefined`. For `jsonObject` it parses the schema and requires `type === 'object'` before calling `onConfirm`.
`config.ts` now ships a full-schema placeholder that matches the editor, and `jsonObjectWrap` is no longer used by the modal.
Backend (unchanged): `VariableEntity` validates the stored string with Draft-7, and `StartNode` validates runtime JSON input against it before the workflow runs.

findings.title: `return True` is an undefined identifier and breaks the TypeScript build
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/index.tsx`, `handleJSONSchemaChange` (around lines 130-144) ends the success path with `return True`. `True` is undefined and will fail type-checking and throw a ReferenceError that the catch block swallows. Remove the `return True` and the unused `const v = JSON.parse(value)` binding; keep the `JSON.parse` as a validity check and call `handlePayloadChange('json_schema')(value)` after it. Keep the existing empty-string branch and the `catch { return null }`.

findings.title: Invalid JSON typed into the schema editor is silently discarded on save
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/index.tsx`, `handleJSONSchemaChange` (lines 130-144) drops invalid JSON, so the editor's text and `tempPayload.json_schema` diverge. Confirm (`handleConfirm`, lines 310-323) then validates the stale previous schema and silently saves it, which makes the `jsonSchemaInvalid` toast unreachable. Change the handler to always store the raw text in `tempPayload.json_schema`. Make sure the `jsonSchemaStr` memo (lines 81-91) does not reset the editor while the text is invalid. Keep the existing `handleConfirm` validation as the single place that reports errors.

findings.title: No tests added for the new JSON Schema behaviour
findings.body:
The PR checklist says "I've added a test for each change", but the diff touches no spec files. No `config-modal` spec exists, and `config-var/index.spec.tsx` does not exercise the JSON branch.

Untested behaviour introduced here:
- `handleConfirm` for `jsonObject`: empty schema maps to `undefined`, non-object `type` is rejected, invalid JSON is rejected.
- `handleJSONSchemaChange`: empty and whitespace-only input clears the field, valid input is stored.
- The `JSON_OBJECT` option is shown for advanced-chat and workflow apps and hidden for basic apps.

The `return True` compile error above would have been caught by any test of this file.

::code{file="web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/index.tsx" lines="248-329"}
findings.fixPrompt: Add a Vitest/RTL spec at `web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/index.spec.tsx` for `ConfigModal`. Cover: (1) JSON_OBJECT option is listed for advanced-chat/workflow apps and absent for basic apps; (2) typing valid schema JSON saves it; (3) whitespace-only schema is saved as undefined; (4) a schema whose `type` is not `object` shows the `jsonSchemaMustBeObject` toast and does not call onConfirm; (5) invalid JSON shows `jsonSchemaInvalid` and does not call onConfirm. Follow the mocking style used by the sibling `config-var/index.spec.tsx`. Assert on onConfirm arguments and toast calls, not internal state.

findings.title: Unused local `normalizedJsonSchema` in handleConfirm
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/index.tsx` `handleConfirm` (around line 251), the `normalizedJsonSchema` constant is never used; the payload is built from `payloadToSave` on lines 255-257. Remove `normalizedJsonSchema`, or derive `payloadToSave` from it so there is a single source of truth for the empty-schema rule. Keep behaviour identical.

findings.title: `jsonObjectWrap` is now an unused export
findings.body:
The modal stopped importing `jsonObjectWrap` when it switched to storing the full schema. Nothing else in `web/` references it, so the export is dead code. Remove it so future readers do not assume it still shapes the saved schema.

::code{file="web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/config.ts" lines="1-6"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `web/app/components/app/configuration/config-var/config-modal/config.ts`, the `jsonObjectWrap` export (lines 1-6) is no longer imported after the index.tsx change in this PR. Grep `web/` to confirm no remaining references, then delete the export. Keep `jsonConfigPlaceHolder` unchanged.

findings.title: Frontend shows and validates the full schema, matching the backend
findings.body:
Removing the `isSupportJSON` gate exposes the option for advanced-chat and workflow apps, as the PR intends. The editor now shows and stores the complete JSON Schema, not only `properties`. Both the placeholder and the editor describe the same shape, so users no longer have to learn a hidden wrapper.

The `type === 'object'` check in `handleConfirm` is a stricter subset of what the backend accepts. `VariableEntity.validate_json_schema` runs Draft-7 `check_schema`, and `StartNode` validates runtime JSON against the same schema. Enforcing `object` at the UI matches the PR's stated goal and fails early.
